context: Two Jhourney retreats (4 days, then 2.5 days), 2024
method: Relax deeply (almost to sleep); bring to mind a person or memory that sparks joy (her child); let the joy loop, pulsing more if it fades; stay without doing anything
time_to_first_jhana: About 2.25 cumulative hours, day 1 (J2; J1 possibly earlier)
outcome: Reached J1-J8 and cessation in about 20 hours
just_before_entry: Deeply relaxed, then holding a joyful image
click_description: Tingling in hands and chest as the sign; the key was something like flow state rather than relaxation alone
blockers: did not trust the experience at first
state_descriptions: J1 euphoric and bright; J2 gratitude, beaming; J3 content and soft; J4 stillness, dissociative; formless states progressively emptier
aftereffects: Better control of attention; less bothered by hard moments; no urge to keep practising after cessation
adverse: Overwhelming moments; left both retreats early to process; advises not doing this isolated
notes: Fastest account collected. Top advice: relax, have fun, do not overthink. Self-reported, single author

prior_experience: About a year of daily practice
blockers: discouraged on learning most others had reached it
aftereffects: Reinvigorated practice; took away that sits should end relaxed and joyful
notes: Estimates about 75% of attendees reached jhana, including near-novices; notes some arrived already able to. The clearest non-responder account: an experienced meditator who failed where novices succeeded

context: Solo home practice from a book
click_description: The deepest event came unexpectedly during breathing exercises, when not trying
notes: Onset when not striving

context: TWIM retreat; later spontaneous deep jhana
outcome: Reached sutta-style jhanas (TWIM) and Visuddhimagga-style jhanas
state_descriptions: Deep jhanas boost sensory clarity and concentration much more
notes: Warns that a fast, startup framing sets up craving and comparison, which are themselves obstacles

click_description: Joy and happiness that settle into stable, calm contentment not dependent on anything external; thoughts fade and disappear
aftereffects: Sense of needing nothing to be content; saw how much effort goes into protecting a model of the world
notes: A careful reporter who withholds the label: useful as a model of calibrated self-report

blockers: existential dread, sadness and anxiety after a couple of days
adverse: Low mood lasting days to weeks after each attempt
notes: Not jhana-specific, but shows that quiet can surface distress in some people. Motivates the app's emotion branch and safety text

method: Slow body scan; pleasure kept in secondary attention; four 15-minute sits each followed by written reflection
time_to_first_jhana: About 9 months of inconsistent practice; under 10 hours of sitting
just_before_entry: Not chasing the pleasure; treating jhana like falling asleep: arrange conditions and let it happen
blockers: a lot of frustration from trying to grasp jhana
could reach some piti but not jhana
aftereffects: Energy after a jhana sit can persist into the next morning
adverse: Sleep disrupted for a night or two after strong sits
notes: Failure modes named: grasping, aversion, frustration (stop for the day), over-contracted attention (loosen, or use a pleasant memory)

context: Month-long retreat plus long solo practice
outcome: Reached jhanas, unreliably; later only brief re-entry
notes: The slow tail: three orders of magnitude more hours than the fastest account. Sceptical of overclaiming; suggests giving up on short-term pursuit can be wise

click_description: Body boundaries dissolving; 'liquid' rather than bright or pleasant
notes: A false positive candidate: strong altered state without the pleasure. Notes priming by instructions may shape what is experienced

context: Solo practice with some personal instruction
method: Find a pleasant sensation, attend narrowly until a feedback loop builds; small attentional shifts between stages
click_description: Access came from getting over self-hatred, not from years of concentration training
blockers: inner critic saying he was doing it wrong, would never get there, or did not deserve pleasure
state_descriptions: J1 sharp, tingly, electric, like sustained orgasm; J2-J3 progressively more relaxed; J4 restful more than pleasurable
aftereffects: Afterglow became monotonous; moved to other practices after about two months
notes: Explicitly describes a feedback loop. Self-criticism as a blocker in its own right

blockers: grasping pushed the pleasure away in early attempts
state_descriptions: First jhana can be agitating: too much pleasure
notes: Independent report of grasping as the early obstacle, and of J1 as over-stimulating

aftereffects: No strong effect on the rest of the day
notes: A deflationary success: real but modest

state_descriptions: Deep first jhana like a full-body orgasm lasting minutes
notes: Depth depends on retreat conditions even for an expert

outcome: Disputed: teachers said jhana, he found it only 'kinda nice'
state_descriptions: Kinda nice; not more bliss than ever experienced
notes: Label inflation from the teacher side: the same state called jhana by teachers and unremarkable by the practitioner

blockers: got distracted and did not keep up the practice
notes: Attrition, the most ordinary failure mode

context: Monastery practice; nine years later a 12-day Pa-Auk retreat
method: Breath at the nostrils to nimitta (Pa-Auk)
time_to_first_jhana: Touched J1 for seconds within months; stable only on a 12-day retreat at 14-20 hours a day
state_descriptions: Non-dual absorption; breath sensation disappears; no voluntary exit
notes: The deep path: far greater dose. Fear at the vanishing breath is a named threshold obstacle

blockers: frustration from trying to grasp jhana: could get piti but not jhana
notes: A teacher's own account of the grasping failure (seen as a search snippet only)

time_to_first_jhana: Within a few days of the retreat
notes: Second-hand, reported by a founder; consistent with experience not predicting success

state_descriptions: Far more pleasurable than other pleasures (his estimate: 10-100x)
aftereffects: Reduced craving for pleasure; rarely practises and often forgets it is available
notes: The most enthusiastic account. No acquisition details. Others in FP3 report no change in desires
